chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife during a period of purity without sexual intercourse, then returns to her on the same day, then divorces her again, so that three divorces are completed in one period of purity. He said: 'He acted contrary to the Sunnah.' I said: 'So it is not befitting for him, when he returns to her, to divorce her except in another period of purity?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Until he has intercourse with her?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.تَبِين: To become manifest/effective (referring to the completion of the count)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for a triple divorce to be valid according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential distinction between a valid triple divorce and an irregular one by emphasizing the necessity of separating the pronouncements across distinct periods of purity (tuhr) with sexual intercourse (jima') in between. It highlights the concept of 'khalaq al-sunnah' (deviating from the Prophetic tradition) when a husband attempts to effectuate three divorces in a single cycle without the requisite consummation, a key point of divergence from some Sunni schools. The dialogue underscores that mere verbal declaration without the physical act of intimacy does not constitute a complete, effective divorce in this specific context.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorced his wife during (her being) clean without copulating with her. Then he returned to her from that day. Then divorced her, manifesting from it with three divorces during one purity’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Opposite to the Sunnah’. I said, ‘So is it not befitting for him when he returns to her that he should divorce her except during another purity?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Until he sleeps with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 12. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, (Musa), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife in a menses-free period during which he has not gone to bed with her. He then goes back to her on the same day, then divorces her: if it becomes irrevocable with three divorces during one menses-free period. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has opposed the Sunnah.’ I then asked, ‘Is it necessary after going back to his wife to divorce her in another menses-free period of time?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, it is necessary.’ I said, ‘So that he can go to bed with her?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, he can do so.”’
